content.value_statement: Playwright suites often become flaky, slow, and noisy in agent workflows. This skill gives practical patterns for reliable tests, reusable setup, and concise CI output.
actual_capabilities: Ranks Playwright locator strategies from user-facing selectors to last-resort CSS and XPath.
Explains web-first assertions that reduce flakiness through automatic waiting.
Shows page object, fixture, and worker fixture patterns for TypeScript suites.
Documents auth state reuse, API login setup, and per-test isolation.
Covers network mocking, HAR replay, and response modification patterns.
Recommends concise Playwright reporters for CLI agents and CI jobs.
limitations: It does not run tests or inspect a live application by itself.
Examples are TypeScript-focused and may require adaptation for other languages.
It does not create complete project scaffolding without additional user instructions.
It cannot verify app-specific selectors, accounts, or API contracts without repository context.

use_cases.title: Stabilize a flaky test
use_cases.description: Review a failing Playwright test and replace fragile waits or selectors with reliable patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize test architecture
use_cases.description: Create consistent page objects, fixtures, and helpers for a growing Playwright suite.

use_cases.title: Reduce CI noise
use_cases.description: Configure reporters, retries, workers, traces, and screenshots for concise agent-friendly output.

prompt_templates.title: Review New Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Playwright test for resilient locators, web-first assertions, isolation, and reporter settings. Suggest direct fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Flaky Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this flaky Playwright flow to remove fixed waits, improve locators, and add reliable assertions. Keep behavior unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Design Fixture Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Playwright fixtures for this suite. Include auth reuse, data cleanup, and per-test isolation. Explain where each file belongs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Suite Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Playwright suite architecture for page objects, worker fixtures, network mocks, CI reporters, and trace settings. Prioritize changes by risk.

output_examples.input: A checkout test uses fixed waits and CSS selectors.
output: Replace fixed waits with assertions on visible checkout states.
Use role, label, or test id locators for each interaction.
Keep one checkout record per test to avoid order dependence.

output_examples.input: A suite logs in through the UI before every test.
output: Move authentication into a setup project or API login helper.
Reuse stored auth state for browser projects.
Keep stored auth files out of version control.

output_examples.input: CI output is too verbose for a coding agent.
output: Use a concise line or dot reporter in agent and CI contexts.
Keep traces and screenshots focused on failures and retries.
Limit workers when CI stability matters more than speed.

best_practices: Prefer role, label, text, alt text, title, and test id locators before CSS or XPath.
Use web-first assertions so Playwright waits for user-visible states.
Keep tests isolated with fixtures, per-test data, and reusable auth state.
anti_patterns: Using fixed timeouts to cover asynchronous UI changes.
Sharing mutable IDs or records across independent tests.
Logging in through the UI in every test when auth state can be reused.

faq.question: Does this skill run Playwright tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The host agent may run tests when the user asks.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it generate page object models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes page object and base page patterns for TypeScript Playwright projects.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation. Its examples include local and application API testing patterns.

faq.question: How does it help CI workflows?
faq.answer: It recommends concise reporters, retries, worker settings, traces, screenshots, and video policies.

faq.question: How should credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Use test-only accounts, environment variables, and gitignored auth state files.
